Others (14%) | chairman = [[Antonio Percassi]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Maurizio Sarri]] | league = {{Italian football updater|Atalanta}} | season = {{Italian football updater|Atalanta2}} | position = {{Italian football updater|Atalanta3}} | current = 2026–27 Atalanta BC season | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _atalanta2627h | pattern_b1 = _atalanta2627h | pattern_ra1 = _atalanta2627h | pattern_sh1 = _atalanta2627h | pattern_so1 = _atalanta2627hl | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _atalanta2627a | pattern_b2 = _atalanta2627a | pattern_ra2 = _atalanta2627a | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = _atalanta2627al | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _atalanta2627t | pattern_b3 = _atalanta2627t | pattern_ra3 = _atalanta2627t | pattern_sh3 = _atalanta2627t | pattern_so3 = _atalanta2627tl | leftarm3 = ff8f00 | body3 = ff8f00 | rightarm3 = ff8f00 | shorts3 = ff8f00 | socks3 = ff8f00 }} '''Atalanta Bergamasca Calcio''' ({{IPA|it|ataˈlanta berɡaˈmaska ˈkaltʃo|lang}}), commonly referred to as '''Atalanta''', is a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Bergamo]], [[Lombardy]], Italy, that competes in [[Serie A]], the top tier of the [[Italian football league system]]. Founded in 1907, Atalanta holds the record for having played the most Serie A seasons (65) without being based in a [[regions of Italy|regional]] capital and without having won the league title. Furthermore, the club holds the record for most promotions to Serie A,{{Efn|Thirteen times, the first in 1927–28 and the latest in 2010–11.}} and also that for the joint-most [[Serie B]] titles, alongside [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]]. Atalanta won the [[Coppa Italia]] in [[1962–63 Coppa Italia|1963]] and the [[UEFA Europa League]] in [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|2024]].{{cite web |date=22 May 2024 |title=Atalanta win the 2023/24 UEFA Europa League: Meet the champions |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0285-18dfede344d4-8ebefb1dffd1-1000--meet-the-2024-winners/ |access-date=22 May 2024 |publisher=[[UEFA]]}} The club qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League]] five times, reaching the quarter-finals in [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|2020]], and participated in six seasons of the UEFA Europa League (previously known as the UEFA Cup).{{efn|This includes one appearance in the knockout stage after a group-stage elimination in the same season's Champions League.}} Atalanta also reached the semi-finals of the [[Cup Winners' Cup]] in [[1987–88 European Cup Winners' Cup|1988]], when it was competing in Serie B. This is still the joint-best performance ever by a non-first division club in a major [[UEFA]] competition.{{efn|Together with [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]}} The club plays its home games at the [[Stadio Atleti Azzurri d'Italia|New Balance Arena]] and its main kit colors are black and blue. Atalanta had a long-standing rivalry with nearby club [[Brescia Calcio]] until that team's dissolution in 2025; the rivalry continues with [[Brescia]]'s [[Phoenix club (sports)|phoenix club]], [[Union Brescia]]. The club is also famed for its [[Atalanta BC Youth Sector|youth academy]], which has produced several notable talents who have played in the top leagues of Europe.{{cite web|date=16 December 2016|title=How AC Milan and Others Have Benefitted from Atalanta's Production Line|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2682063-how-ac-milan-and-others-have-benefitted-from-atalantas-production-line|website=bleacherreport.com|access-date=31 January 2021}}"}}
